items.stem: At the commencement of a lease, how does a lessee generally measure the lease liability?

options.text: At the present value of the lease payments not yet paid, discounted at the rate implicit in the lease or the incremental borrowing rate
options.rationale: Correct: the liability is the discounted outstanding lease payments.

options.text: At the undiscounted total of all lease payments over the term
options.rationale: The liability is discounted, not the undiscounted total.

options.text: At the fair value of the underlying asset
options.rationale: The liability is based on the lease payments, not the asset's fair value.

options.text: At zero until the first payment is made
options.rationale: The liability is recognised at commencement.

items.explanation: Correct: the liability is the discounted outstanding lease payments.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO leases may a lessee elect not to recognise on the balance sheet under the recognition exemptions? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A short-term lease of 12 months or less with no purchase option
options.rationale: Correct: short-term leases qualify for the exemption.

options.text: A lease of a low-value underlying asset
options.rationale: Correct: low-value asset leases qualify for the exemption.

options.text: A 10-year lease of a core distribution centre
options.rationale: A long-term lease of a significant asset does not qualify.

options.text: A lease with a bargain purchase option the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise
options.rationale: Such a lease is not short-term and does not qualify.

items.explanation: Correct: short-term leases qualify for the exemption.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A lessee argues that because it depreciates the right-of-use asset on a straight-line basis and the liability unwinds using the effective-interest method, the asset and liability will stay equal each year. Why is this wrong?

options.text: The two balances follow different patterns, so the right-of-use asset and the lease liability diverge over the lease term
options.rationale: Correct: straight-line depreciation and effective-interest unwinding produce different carrying amounts.

options.text: The right-of-use asset is never depreciated
The lease liability is remeasured to fair value each year
options.rationale: The liability is measured at amortised cost, not fair value.

options.text: Both are always written down to zero immediately
options.rationale: Neither is written off at commencement.

items.explanation: Correct: straight-line depreciation and effective-interest unwinding produce different carrying amounts.
